findings.reason: The protected source is a clear direct grammar validator. It distinguishes the delimiter families, preserves empty split fields for rejection, checks every IPv4 lexical and numeric rule, admits exactly the required IPv6 alphabet and field widths, and returns the contract literals without unnecessary abstraction, so no inert candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 468 and its queryIP-to-classification Python contract. Splitting and validating collectively scan and store O(n) characters, supporting the manifest's O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary-space claims.

The immutable native source is bound to verified submission 2064962311. It is identical to the protected source in delimiter selection, field counts, nonempty and width tests, ASCII-decimal enforcement, leading-zero and 255 checks, IPv6 alphabet construction, per-character validation, and every return path; only the LeetCode class wrapper differs.

The malformed strings of lengths 16, 64, and 100 span more than 6x and make structural rejection scan the complete input. The current source passed all 7 opaque correctness executions and all three performance tiers at 1.02x the reference runtime. A correct control that redundantly reparses every growing prefix passed every opaque correctness execution and every benchmark output but failed only the runtime verdict at 6.73x.

The Approach exactly describes the protected branch order and predicates, including split-preserved empty fields, the ASCII guard before Python digit conversion, IPv4 leading-zero semantics, full eight-field IPv6 syntax, case-insensitive hexadecimal characters, mixed delimiters, and the linear split-storage bound.

The hash-bound modular Reference was checked directly against the live public statement. It restores the complete IPv4 and IPv6 grammar narratives, all nine source-native valid and invalid address illustrations, all three canonical examples with explanations, the sole input-alphabet constraint, and the absence of tables, visuals, or later statement sections.
